scene: Three cartoon people in ragged brown clothing occupy a sandy prehistoric setting. A frowning person at left holds hands with a braided person in the middle, whose eyes are red hearts and whose other hand touches their cheek. A muscular person at right flexes one arm and rests the other hand on their waist. Rocks, a wooden structure, a palm tree and a small skull appear behind or beside them.
mechanism: The handholding pair and the heart-eyed middle figure looking toward the flexing person create a visual relationship triangle. ONLY ONE? frames exclusivity as the unanswered question.
mechanism_secondary: comparison between the frowning partner and the flexing alternative
composition: Large yellow words occupy the top quarter. Three separated faces form a horizontal chain below; the muscular right figure is the largest body. The handholding gesture links the left pair while the middle figure's gaze connects to the right. Small environmental props sit near the lower corners.
typography: Two uppercase yellow words with heavy black outlines span almost the full width. ONLY ONE? remains readable at 320x180 and 160x90. No other legible words or incidental scene text are present.
colors: Orange sky and yellow light contrast with brown ground and clothing. White faces and the muscular torso separate strongly from the warm background; red heart eyes and a red scribble provide small emotional accents, rather than a warning banner.
psychology: The left face has angled brows and a downturned mouth; the middle face has heart-shaped eyes and a slight smile. The right face has lowered eyelids and an upturned mouth beside a flexing pose. These stylized cues suggest attraction and rivalry without establishing actual historical behavior.
partnership: The title asks broadly how ancient humans managed relationships. The image narrows this to exclusivity and rival attraction, adding a concrete social dilemma while leaving the historical answer unstated. The cartoon is illustrative rather than evidence about ancient relationships.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: ONLY ONE? is likely read first, followed by the large flexing body, the heart eyes and finally the left person's frown and the linked hands.
art: Bold black-outlined cartoon characters use flat white faces, brown hair and clothing over a lightly shaded landscape. The repeated outline style is coherent; exaggerated anatomy and heart eyes signal a comic illustration, not historical documentation.
strength: The large two-word question and three distinct expressions survive mobile reduction and make the relationship tension quick to recognize.
weakness: The muscular rival dominates the image and can narrow a broad relationship-history topic into a generic romantic competition joke.
bottleneck: The image establishes a rivalry but gives no distinctive historical practice or artifact to differentiate the promised explanation.
action: HYPOTHESIS: replace one minor landscape prop with a historically sourced relationship-practice cue while retaining the readable question and three-person arrangement.
counterexample: NOT_ASSIGNED: low public performance alone does not establish a packaging-performance counterexample; cohort and temporal-alignment limitations remain.
expression_label: angled brows and frown / heart eyes and smile / lowered eyelids and slight smile
hero_object: flexing cartoon figure beside a handholding pair

scene: An outlined illustration shows pastel waterfront buildings receding along a cobbled street, palm trees, steep mountains at left and blue sea at right. Very small human-like figures appear near the middle-distance buildings; their exact count and features are not reliably distinguishable. Large black CAPE VERDE and a date range occupy the open sky.
mechanism: Recognizable destination imagery and a long date span signal a complete national-history overview. The attractive coast supports the title's paradise framing, but the image does not introduce a specific historical tension.
mechanism_secondary: specificity through named place and date span
composition: The street and building line recede diagonally from the bottom left toward the central shoreline. Open sky in the upper right reserves a clean area for the place name and dates. Mountains fill the upper left and the sea balances the right half; no single person dominates.
typography: CAPE VERDE is a large heavy black serif headline; 1460 – 2026 is smaller bold black text directly beneath it. Both lines remain readable at 320x180 and 160x90, although the dates become secondary. No incidental in-scene text is verifiable.
colors: Light cyan sky and blue sea surround yellow, mint, pink and blue facades. Dark outlines separate the buildings, and black text contrasts against the uncluttered sky. The palette is calm and scenic, with no red warning treatment.
psychology: The image offers scenery rather than a readable face or emotional pose. Tiny human-like marks are insufficient for expression analysis; the viewer appeal is an inviting coastal setting, an analyst interpretation rather than observed emotion.
partnership: The title promises the entire history in seven minutes and describes a strange Atlantic paradise. The image repeats the destination and adds a 1460–2026 span and scenic setting; it does not communicate what is strange or unknown. The dates are visible copy, not independently verified historical endpoints.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the black place name is likely noticed before the date range; the eye then follows the colorful facades down the street toward the sea. Small figures contribute little at mobile size.
art: Consistent black outlines and lightly shaded flat colors produce an illustrated travel-poster appearance. Perspective draws the town into the distance while mountains and shoreline form a continuous background. This is a stylized setting, not a documented photograph of a specific street.
strength: The open sky gives the country name exceptional separation, while the waterfront illustration quickly signals a destination-history video.
weakness: A scenic town and broad date range make the package look like a conventional overview; the title's strange-paradise hook receives little visual support.
bottleneck: The image names the subject but leaves the distinctive historical question entirely to the long title.
action: HYPOTHESIS: substitute one clearly sourced historical turning-point symbol for a minor scenic detail to communicate why this destination's story is unusual.
counterexample: NOT_ASSIGNED: a middle public-performance class and analyst score do not by themselves establish a counterexample.
expression_label: not resolvable in tiny distant figures
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

text: ISRAEL / 37 BC – 2026 [incidental architectural band marks: TEXT_PRESENT_BUT_NOT_VERIFIABLE]
scene: A stylized cityscape of pale stone buildings, walls and green trees surrounds a large gold-domed building with blue patterned walls on the left. A smaller gray dome and towers appear farther right. ISRAEL and 37 BC – 2026 are printed in black against an open light-blue sky. The blue architectural bands have tiny decorative or text-like marks whose characters cannot be established. No person is clearly distinguishable.
mechanism: The large place label and conspicuous golden dome provide subject recognition; the date range signals a broad historical timeline. There is no depicted conflict, transformation or specific unanswered event beyond the overview premise.
composition: The golden dome is the dominant image on the left, balanced by a large headline and dates in the upper right. The lower half is densely filled with city walls, rooftops and trees. Clean sky prevents the text from competing with the detailed architecture.
typography: A black serif ISRAEL headline sits above bold 37 BC – 2026. Both remain readable at 320x180 and 160x90. Tiny marks in the building's blue bands are incidental and not verifiable as exact text at native size; they are excluded from the prominent four-token count.
colors: The golden dome contrasts with cyan sky and blue architectural ornament. Pale tan buildings and deep green trees fill the foreground. Black copy remains strongly separated from sky; there is no red warning treatment.
psychology: No readable human face or pose supplies emotional information. Monumental architecture may imply historical significance to a viewer, but that is an analyst inference rather than a visible emotion or documented account of the location.
partnership: The title offers the entire history of Israel in twelve minutes. The image repeats the place label and adds a date span and architectural scene. It does not show the event sequence or clarify how the video's historical scope relates to the region, state or landmark. The visible dates are packaging copy, not verified chronology.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the gold dome and black ISRAEL headline compete for first attention; the dates follow. The lower cityscape becomes texture at mobile size rather than a sequence of individually meaningful buildings.
art: Black outlines, flat shading and repeated window details create an illustrated architectural panorama. The gold dome has simple curved grid lines and the blue bands carry miniature ornament. Fine background detail is coherent visually but loses definition after reduction.
strength: A large isolated country label and a bright gold landmark create strong recognition even when the city details shrink.
weakness: The architectural panorama is static and does little to distinguish this overview from another broad history or destination video.
bottleneck: The thumbnail offers a place and timeline without a concrete historical tension, leaving the entire-history promise broad and difficult to differentiate.
action: HYPOTHESIS: introduce one documented historical turning point as a secondary focal cue while preserving the high-contrast subject label and gold dome.
counterexample: NOT_ASSIGNED: the LOW cohort class is measured at only 1.5 days of reported age; it cannot alone establish a reliable packaging-performance counterexample.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

scene: On a cream background, a large black glass pyramid at the left has a white light beam shooting straight up from its apex. In front of it sits a sphinx statue with a striped headdress on a gold entrance block, flanked by rows of palm trees. A fairytale castle with red, blue and white spires stands at the far left edge behind the palms. At the lower right, a strip of hotel towers and a street forms a skyline, and a thin red arrow links the two years under the headline. Small sign-like marks occur in the lower-right cityscape and along the cropped foreground roof; their exact lettering is not verifiable.
mechanism: A landmark postcard with a time span: the pyramid, sphinx, castle and towers stand in for a city, and the 1905-to-2026 arrow frames a whole-history timeline.
composition: The pyramid takes the left half with its apex in the upper-left quadrant, and the headline block takes the right half at upper right. The skyline strip runs low across the right, so the layout reads as scenery on the left, text on the right and a horizontal city band underneath. The vertical light beam splits the cream sky.
typography: Four tokens in two tiers: LAS VEGAS in large black condensed capitals, with 1905 and 2026 joined by a thin red arrow beneath. The two years are also readable at 160x90. The title already gives the subject and a 13-minute length, and the thumbnail adds the start and end years. PROMINENT_PACKAGE_TEXT: LAS VEGAS / 1905 / 2026. INCIDENTAL_IN_SCENE_TEXT: TEXT_PRESENT_BUT_NOT_VERIFIABLE; tiny signage is excluded from the four-token count.
colors: A warm cream field carries black text and a black pyramid with gold and sandy accents, a small blue-and-red castle and one red arrow. The low-saturation parchment look contrasts the black pyramid sharply.
psychology: No living human figure is distinguishable. The sphinx statue has a drawn face, which is an architectural motif rather than a human emotional signal. Landmark spectacle and broad historical scope are analyst interpretations.
partnership: The title promises the entire history in 13 minutes, and the thumbnail turns the claim into a 1905-to-2026 arrow and a landmark scene. It complements the title with the year range, but the images show only modern buildings, so nothing from 1905 appears. The printed dates are packaging copy, not verified historical endpoints; content coverage remains NOT_CHECKED.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the black pyramid and its beam first, then LAS VEGAS at upper right, then the 1905-to-2026 line, and finally the skyline strip at lower right.
art: Clean flat illustration with bold outlines and a coherent cream-and-black palette, and the sphinx, palms and castle are consistent in style. Background detail on the right skyline is dense but small, while the large pyramid shape survives at 160x90.
strength: The pyramid silhouette and strongly separated LAS VEGAS label remain clear at 160x90; landmark recognition depends on viewer familiarity.
weakness: The timeline supplies two dates but the scene offers no visually separated past-and-present comparison; the historical transformation remains unspecified.
bottleneck: The postcard-style landmark scene has no person or tension, so the frame announces a topic rather than a story.
action: Hypothesis: add a small desert-town scene under 1905 beside the skyline under 2026, to test whether a visible before-and-after pair makes the time span concrete.
counterexample: NOT_ASSIGNED: the legacy Seq 5 comparison was not identified and matched here; public performance does not establish packaging causality.
hero_object: black pyramid with light beam and sphinx
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

scene: Two outlined cartoon figures flank large white text over a world map. At left, an older balding figure in a dark suit holds a smoking cigar with a frowning face. At right, a red-coated soldier wears a tall black hat and holds a long gun with a bayonet. Red and gray regions contrast against dark blue seas.
mechanism: The huge 1600 YEARS claim and small viewing commitment promise compressed historical scope; opposed civilian and soldier figures frame empire through recognizable visual types.
composition: White 1600 YEARS occupies the center in two oversized lines; IN 10 MINUTES sits below. Figures bracket the text at both edges. The background map extends across the canvas but its borders are partly covered.
typography: PROMINENT_PACKAGE_TEXT: 1600 YEARS / IN 10 MINUTES. Five bold white tokens with heavy black outlines remain readable at 320x180 and 160x90. No incidental lettering is verifiable; small hat and uniform marks are decorative motifs.
colors: Dark blue sea and gray land contrast with red map fills and the red coat. White faces and lettering provide strong foreground separation. Red denotes visual emphasis and map regions, not a warning banner.
psychology: The left figure has lowered angular brows, a downturned mouth and creased cheeks; the soldier has dot eyes and a small flat mouth. These visible cues support a stern-versus-neutral interpretation. A Churchill resemblance is inference, not verified identity.
partnership: The title names the British Empire and promises its entire history. The image supplies 1600 YEARS and IN 10 MINUTES, plus map and military imagery. The 1600-year claim extends scope substantially; historical accuracy and actual runtime are not verified from packaging.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: 1600 YEARS likely dominates first attention, followed by the white faces, IN 10 MINUTES and red map regions. This is an inspection heuristic, not an eye-tracking result.
art: Thick black outlines, simplified white faces and flat color fills unify the figures with the illustrated map. The left face has more anatomical detail than the soldier; borders and uniform decorations reduce to texture on mobile.
strength: The central scope claim remains legible at 160x90, and two large figures create a clear frame for the text.
weakness: The prominently stated 1600-year scope lacks an explained starting point and can confuse what history the British Empire title covers.
bottleneck: The strongest visual promise is a large duration claim whose relationship to the named empire is unspecified.
action: HYPOTHESIS: replace the unexplained span with a sourced scope or turning-point phrase and test clarity without changing the strong text hierarchy.
counterexample: NOT_ASSIGNED: assess public-performance versus analyst-score disagreement only after channel comparison; no causal inference.
expression_label: left frown and angled brows; right neutral mouth
hero_object: oversized 1600 YEARS text between civilian and soldier
